articles.summary: Toluca FC overcame Club de Fútbol Monterrey Rayados A.C. to win the Leagues Cup final 2-0 at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston, on Sunday.
articles.body:
Toluca FC overcame Club de Fútbol Monterrey Rayados A.C. to win the Leagues Cup final 2-0 at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston, on Sunday.

As the first non-MLS team to win the Cup since 2021, when León took home the honors, Toluca became the third Liga MX team to win it all, bringing the MLS-Liga MX battle to a 3-3 count all time since the tournament's inaugural edition in 2019.

The four MLS teams to make it out of Phase One fell short in the knockout bracket, all losing to their Liga MX opponents in the quarterfinals to make way for an all-Liga MX semifinal.

Club Leon (LEO) def. Real Salt Lake (RSL), 3-0

Toluca FC (TOL) def. Austin FC (ATX), 2-0

Club de Futbol Monterrey Rayados A.C (MTY) def. Chicago Fire FC (CHI), 2-1

Club America (AME) def. Columbus Crew (CLB), 2-0

It took little time for Toluca forward Alexis Vega to get the team on the board, scoring in the fourth minute.

Vega followed up on a missed shot, sneaking past a defender before firing one into the bottom-right corner of the goal.

Three players received yellow cards in the first half, two for Toluca and one for Monterrey. Toluca missed one attempt while three were saved, while Monterrey missed four and had three saved.

Coming out of the break, Monterrey needed to make something happen to get back into the game, failing to execute on any of their shots on goal in the first half.

Instead, it was Toluca forward Helio Nunes who found the back of the net in the 70th minute, capitalizing on a blocked shot from the Monterrey goalkeeper to give Toluca a 2-0 advantage.

Monterrey could not make up the difference during regulation or the additional six minutes of stoppage time, allowing Toluca to walk away with the Leagues Cup win.

articles.title: Bayern Munich News: PSG, Real Madrid using intermediaries to chat with FC Bayern’s Michael Olise; Bayern eyeing Brentford’s Kevin Schade?; and MORE!
articles.summary: The FC Bayern star has some deep-pocketed suitors in Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid.
articles.body:
Ask a Bayern Munich executive or management figure about French mega-star Michael Olise and he will tell you that the winger is not for sale.

Chief executive officer Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer, board member for sport Max Eberl, sporting director Christoph Freund, and supervisory board member Uli Hoeneß will all give you the same story. One thing that none of them can be completely certain of, however, is the future.

As for that, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly trying to make headway. In this report, the duo is allegedly working through intermediaries to see if a deal can get done at some point:

Following his outstanding performances for FC Bayern Munich and the French national team at the 2026 World Cup, Michael Olise remains on the wish lists of top European clubs. The 24-year-old right winger is one of the key players in Bayern's attack. His contract with the German record champions runs until June 30, 2029. With his strong start to the 2026/27 season, Olise has further cemented his status as a highly sought-after transfer target. Olise's rapid development and consistently strong performances have attracted the attention of Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in particular. According to information from fussball-news.de, both European powerhouses are closely monitoring his progress and are considering high-caliber reinforcements for the right wing and attacking positions. Initial exploratory talks and informal contacts via intermediaries have reportedly already taken place to assess the financial parameters of a potential transfer. However, formal negotiations between the clubs are not yet underway. Bayern Munich generally intend to block any potential offers during the winter transfer window. However, an exceptionally high offer could at least prompt the club to consider it. According to sources, Bayern Munich values ​​Olise at between €200 and €230 million. The salary issue could also play a crucial role in his future. Olise is reportedly seeking to align his wages with top earners Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala. A salary package of around €25 million per year is being discussed. Therefore, it could be decisive whether Bayern Munich can reconcile their wage structure with the player's demands. Scouts from PSG and Real Madrid are expected to continue closely monitoring Olise in the coming months. Should the financial expectations of the parties involved converge, the Bayern star's future could become one of the major topics of the 2027 winter transfer window.

Baza is…16! Kid looks like he is 12! Wow. Good for him. He will appreciate his youth appearance when he gets older.

articles.title: Takeaways from College Football Week 1: Mayhem in Michigan, concerns in Clemson
articles.summary: College football is back with all of its wildness and drama.
articles.body:
College football is unpredictable and delightful, which is why we live for what happens on Saturdays. And Week 1 absolutely delivered, from an extremely controversial last-second Hail Mary in Ann Arbor to a stunning beatdown in Baton Rouge and everything in between. Each Sunday, I'll publish my biggest takeaways from the college football weekend. I'll highlight the most interesting storylines, track College Football Playoff contenders and specifically shout out individual and team performances that deserve the spotlight.

1. There were no winners from the debacle at the Big House

Michigan didn't deserve to win on Saturday. It got outplayed and out-physicaled from the start by Western Michigan — and needing that second put back on the clock to throw a second (and, this time, successful) Hail Mary to eke out the win over the Broncos. I don't think I've seen any Michigan fan genuinely happy about that outcome or the state of the Wolverine offense under Bryce Underwood right now.

Western Michigan feels like it got screwed out of what would have been the biggest win in program history. And for general college football fans, there's now less trust in the officiating and replay processes than there was a week ago. There were truly no winners in Ann Arbor on Saturday night.

2. Dabo Swinney's time at Clemson feels like it's running out

A few weeks ago, I made a bold prediction that this would be Dabo Swinney's last season at Clemson. I didn't say whether the school would push him out or he'd be the one to leave because of how frustrated the fan and donor base has become. For the record, I do think it would be extremely difficult for the school to fire a coach who won two national championships and turned little ol' Clemson into a college football power.

Clemson didn't look like it belonged on the same field as LSU on Saturday night, let alone the same category of serious CFP contender. The Tigers, at one point in the third quarter, had a total of -10 rushing yards. It was astonishing to see how far the mighty Clemson program has fallen in less than a decade, and it makes my bold prediction seem far less bold. It has been a long time since Clemson actually was Clemson . I know the Tigers made the CFP (albeit as a three-loss ACC champion) in 2024, but the program has not been contending for national titles since the start of the NIL era (in 2021).

Dabo has famously been slow to adapt to the changing landscape of college football, resistant to both the transfer portal and the NIL/revenue-sharing realm. He's repeatedly made bad hires (and hamstrung potential innovators he did bring in from the outside) while accepting complacency.

How else do you explain losing nine NFL draft picks from a 7-6 team and doing nothing to replenish the roster? Bringing back an old friend to run the offense with a quarterback who clearly isn't ready for prime time? And you didn't think to get a different one in the portal instead? Either the Clemson brass is going to have to make a tough call at the end of the season or Dabo will "go somewhere else and coach," as he told us last year amid mounting criticism of his disappointing team. But either way, it's hard to imagine the status quo continuing much longer. It's unacceptable, inexcusable — and an unserious way to run a major college football program.

Curt Cignetti knows how to pick 'em. Quarterback Josh Hoover looked great in his Hoosier debut — blood and all — as did receiver Nick Marsh. For those who didn't watch a lot of Marsh at Michigan State, welcome to the party. He's one of the most electric players in the country.

4. Lane Kiffin has fully embraced his role as college football's biggest villain

Lane Kiffin, like most of us, generally likes to be liked. It clearly bothered him last December when Ole Miss fans hated him for the way he left Oxford, bouncing for LSU instead of coaching the Rebels into the College Football Playoff.

But, after weeks of pushing to try to play ex-NFL players and battling the SEC to do so, Kiffin seemed more at peace with his place in the college football landscape. Up 31-3 on Clemson at the half on Saturday night, Kiffin finished up his ABC interview and muttered, "Imagine if we had pro players." After the game — that ended with an even more lopsided 51-10 final score — Kiffin was asked about the quip.

"What's the difference? Everyone already hates you. They can't hate you that much more," he said. "I'm just glad they played the way they did, so that wouldn't have been the story. Even if we would have won close, it would've been how I screwed the team up doing this thing. "I said this morning [on College Gameday], you can not agree with it. I've been criticized heavily this past week, and I get that and understand, but my job is not to please you and worry about what you are going to write. My job is that I believe in what is right. And I believed in fighting for those kids. … That's what I believe." It's good Lane is ready for whatever comes next — because his return to Oxford is less than two weeks away.

I put Boise State in my preseason CFP bracket because I expected the Broncos to be the highest-ranked Group of 6 champion. That was before Maddux Madsen and Co. nearly upset No. 2 Oregon on the road in their season-opener.

6. Oregon's too-close-for-comfort September win is nothing new.

We've seen the Ducks do this before, most notably two years ago — a 10-point win over Idaho and a three-point win over Boise State — before rolling through the rest of the season, winning a Big Ten title and earning a No. 1 seed in the College Football Playoff.

All that to say, Oregon has a track record of shaky starts and significant in-season improvement. The Ducks were breaking in two new coordinators in this case, too. I'll reserve my right to worry about Oregon, but I won't do so just yet.

The first half against Wisconsin was a bit concerning — largely because of how tight the Irish looked, and how physical the Badgers were — but the second half was a totally different story. Notre Dame put on a clinic and showed flashes of the team that can and should be in the mix for a national championship.

I'd like to see more from the Irish run game, but I also recognize that it's going to be difficult to replace two first-rounders in the backfield, and that may be a work-in-progress for a little while. Notre Dame has time to work out its kinks and figure out how to start games better. I'm really not worried.

8. Baylor got the full DJ Lagway experience

He'll push his body to the limit. He'll throw some darts. But he'll also have some dreadful turnovers and deliver a most painful loss. Woof.

9. The Heisman hopefuls sure look like Heisman Trophy-caliber players.

College football's biggest stars certainly showed up in Week 1. It didn't matter the opponent, these players were ready to play and ready to show out — from Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney at Miami to USC's Jayden Maiava, Ohio State's Julian Sayin-Jeremiah Smith duo, Oregon's Dante Moore, CJ Carr at Notre Dame and more.

10. The SEC won its battle against LSU, and it might win the war, too.

Lane Kiffin opted against listing tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris on the LSU active roster on Friday, despite a Baton Rouge judge clearing the two to return to college football after signing NFL contracts. Kiffin could, theoretically, still add ex-pros later in the fall as long as there are available spots on the 105-man roster (there are) and the players are enrolled in school (they are), but is the juice really worth the squeeze at this point? Does Kiffin really want to risk the severe penalties that the SEC has threatened to levy against a team that rosters ex-pros? Is he willing to risk his own suspension and/or a massive fine? We'll see. Still, it's notable that the SEC's new rules and the league's federal lawsuit filed to support its ability to enforce them was enough to deter Kiffin and Co. for the time being. That's a win for the concept of conference self-governance, and it's a good sign that college football can police itself — at least somewhat.

articles.title: Jaden Thomas' Hat Trick Leads Stanford Over Santa Clara
articles.summary: Stanford ends its non-conference schedule on a high note, led by three goals from Jaden Thomas.
articles.body:
On Thursday night, Stanford women's soccer allowed its first goal of the season against USC. Then it allowed another, and found itself trailing for the first time all season, 2-1, in the 54th minute. That score held until Brooke Holden tied the game at two in the 87th minute, saving the Cardinal from its first loss of the year.

This game came on the heels of a 7-0 win over Cal State Fullerton that boasted seven different scorers. Stanford has also been operating shorthanded, with a number of key pieces playing overseas in the U-20 Women's World Cup.

On Sunday the Cardinal got back to its No. 1 ranked form with a 4-0 win over Santa Clara on the road. Stanford recorded three goals in the first half, first from leading scorer Charlotte Kohler, who notched her sixth of the season in the 8th minute.

The way that Kohler took the pass, created space for herself, and then both drilled and floated her shot with her left boot past the goalkeeper was special and showcased just how quick her striking ability is.

From that point forward, it became the Jaden Thomas show. She was surprised by her big sister before the game, who she has a special connection with.

"That was really emotional for me, being able to get that first goal and have my whole family here to see it," Thomas said after the game. Once we got one [goal], two and three just came after, so it was great."

The junior would record a brace with goals in the 18th and 27th minutes before the half, and then made it a full hat trick with her third goal of the game right out of the half in the 51st minute. She also assisted on Kohler's goal, giving her seven of her eight points on the season in this one game.

Stanford would end up winning this match 4-0, with Thomas having a hand in all four goals. She would end up playing just 56 minutes, but her impact was certainly felt.

Santa Clara ended up with 10 shots, four on goal, which led to Rhiannon Stewart's four saves in net as she earned her third win of the season.

The Cardinal have now finished up the non-conference schedule for this season, and will face No. 2 Duke on the road next Sunday, September 13, before returning home to face Louisville and Wake Forest. The Duke matchup will be an early one on the West Coast, with a 9:00 a.m. PST match time.

Duke is 5-0-1 and defeated USC 3-1 in their first match of the season. Duke's lone tie was a 1-1 draw with UCLA on the road. Stanford won its home match against the Bruins 3-0. This match will be a battle of heavyweights.

"Going into ACC, we just wanted to make a statement to ourselves and the rest of the country," Thomas said. "We are coming, and aiming for that national championship."

articles.title: Xabi Alonso: Arsenal defeat ‘needs to hurt in a positive way’
articles.summary: Post-match reaction from the manager after his first defeat as Chelsea boss
articles.body:
Chelsea tasted defeat under Xabi Alonso for the first time yesterday, losing 2-1 to the defending Premier League champions, Arsenal. Given that this is now our twelfth (12th!) successive match against the Gunners that we've failed to win, losing once again at the Emirates should hardly be a surprise. Obviously, we were hoping for something better, and another fast start gave us real hope, but Arsenal played some brilliant football at times, got some friendly calls at other times, and did what all good champions do: hold a lead and see out an expected win.

As disappointing as it was to walk away with no points, the Blues gave pretty good account of ourselves out there. A bounce here, a bounce there, and the result could've been quite different. Of course, that's scant consolation when it comes to the scoreboard and the standings, but it is a sign of positive progress, especially so early on in the season. This will be one of the toughest challenges we face all season; we can at least take some lessons from it. As cliche as it might be, we can use this defeat to get better. (And in a way, in order to reach our eventual ambitions, we absolutely have to.)

"We are disappointed. It needs to hurt, but it needs to hurt in a positive way, because it's just game three, still many games to play and we know it was going to be a very intense game today." "[We] have done many right things [but] we need to make it better, we need to learn from them, because this is the top level. When we have to play top level, we want to be as efficient and as accurate in all the phases of the game. But this is where we are, this is game three for us of this new start, this new phase that we are starting with Chelsea. But I'm happy with the spirit and the attitude from the players. They have given everything, they have tried and they fought really hard." "My priority is to win games [so] we want to do better, we want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time as well. [It's] going to be a long [season] and [this game] doesn't have a big impact in our mood and in our mindset." -Xabi Alonso; source: Football.London

"We are disappointed. It needs to hurt, but it needs to hurt in a positive way, because it's just game three, still many games to play and we know it was going to be a very intense game today."

"[We] have done many right things [but] we need to make it better, we need to learn from them, because this is the top level. When we have to play top level, we want to be as efficient and as accurate in all the phases of the game. But this is where we are, this is game three for us of this new start, this new phase that we are starting with Chelsea. But I'm happy with the spirit and the attitude from the players. They have given everything, they have tried and they fought really hard."

"My priority is to win games [so] we want to do better, we want to be tighter, to be more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time as well. [It's] going to be a long [season] and [this game] doesn't have a big impact in our mood and in our mindset."

So, basically, it's just one game, just one defeat, and we cannot let that sap our budding momentum. We need to learn from it, get better from it, (get healthier from it), and onwards and upwards we must go. Another big derby coming up midweek, against Leeds United in the League Cup. Perfect time for a response.

articles.title: Toluca wins Leagues Cup with Vega, Helinho scoring to beat Monterrey
articles.summary: The Diablos Rojos added another trophy to the club's impressive case with manager Antonio Mohamed shoring up his place in the team's history.
articles.body:
Alexis Vega scored in the fourth minute with Helinho adding an insurance goal in the 70th minute as the Diablos Rojos beat Monterrey 2-0 Sunday, Sept. 6 in Houston to win the 2026 Leagues Cup final.

In addition to winning the two-bowled trophy awarded to the winner of the tournament that pits Liga MX clubs against their MLS counterparts, Toluca also secures a bye to the round of 16 of the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup . Monterrey and León, which beat Club América earlier Sunday in the third-place game, also qualify to the CCC through the Leagues Cup.

Vega took advantage of lax play from Monterrey to give Toluca an early lead. After a Toluca scoring chance seemed to go wanting when it bounced off the post, Monterrey midfielder Orbelin Pineda had the ball at his feet in the box. He was too slow to clear it, however, and Vega picked his pocket. The Toluca attacker finished off the opening goal with his first touch of the ball, much to the frustration of the pro-Rayados crowd in south Texas.

It was a frenetic start to the match, with a pair of Monterrey scoring chances sandwiched around Vega's opener. Rayados forward Hugo Cuypers put a header just off target in the third minute, and in the sixth minute, Toluca goalkeeper Hugo Gonzalez was able to stop a shot on target from Lucas Ocampos.

But Toluca was able to find success down the wings and limit Monterrey's forays forward for the rest of the half. After a bright start to the second half from Monterrey, Toluca manager Antonio Mohamed responded with four substitutions in quick succession – two in the 61st minute and two in the 68th.

The modifications worked as Helinho scored a vintage Toluca goal, as midfielder Franco Romero surged forward on the counter-attack and set up forward Federico Viñas. The Uruguayan's shot was saved, but Helinho was rewarded for making a back-post run, tapping in the rebound and running off to celebrate his goal.

How many trophies has Antonio Mohamed won with Toluca?

The trophy is another in an impressive stretch under the watch of manager Antonio Mohamed for Toluca, a club based in the city of the same name in the state of Mexico around 40 miles southwest of Mexico City. The Diablos Rojos won back-to-back Liga MX titles in 2025, winning both the Clausura and Apertura – Mexico's short tournaments. They also won the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup, beating Tigres on penalties in the final.

The club also won the 2025 Campeon de Campeones, a preseason match against a fellow Liga MX team, and the 2025 Campeons Cup, a one-off game between the Campeon de Campeones winner and the holder of the MLS Cup. If those two non-major titles are included, Mohamed becomes Toluca's most successful manager all-time with six trophies, passing the legendary Nacho Trelles who led Toluca between 1966 and 1972.

Now, the club can add becoming the first Liga MX club to win the expanded Leagues Cup to its list of achievements. Later this year, it will meet the winner of the 2026 Copa Libertadores in FIFA's Intercontinental Cup, and its CCC title also booked a place in the 2029 Club World Cup should the format stay the same.

For now, it turns its attention back to league play not only having won another trophy but also recuperating one of its biggest stars.

Already leading 2-0, Mohamed brought Paulinho off the bench. in the 78th minute. The Portuguese forward named best player in the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup and top player in Liga MX in 2024–25, hasn't played since the 2026 CCC final after suffering a calf tear.

Toluca returns to league play Saturday, Sept. 12, with a home match against Atlas, the same day Rayados host their crosstown rival Tigres in the Clásico Regio.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: After so many Week 1 blowouts, which team deserves the No. 1 spot?
articles.summary: Notre Dame was a trendy title pick ahead of the college football season, and the Irish looked great on Sunday. But they weren't the only team that impressed...
articles.body:
Notre Dame entered the 2026 season as the trendy pick to make a deep run in the playoff, if not win it all.

The Irish returned 10 starters and their top six tacklers from last year's salty defensive unit, have an experienced and talented guy behind center in CJ Carr and, despite losing two of the best running backs in the country, returned a plethora of dynamic skill players.

Notre Dame cruised to a 41-13 win over Wisconsin at Lambeau Field on Sunday night in a prime-time affair that turned into a rout by the end of the third quarter. Marcus Freeman's team turned a 13-10 halftime lead into a whipping in the second half through a variety pack: a pick-6, a 28-yard touchdown pass and two rushing scores from new featured back Aneyas Williams.

Freeman told NBC in the postgame interview that he and his team were "pressing" during a lackluster first half.

"The offense stayed on track because we had some successful runs," Freeman said. "The establishment of the rushing game really helped us."

The performance sprung Notre Dame into our No. 2 spot in our debut of the Top 10, only behind Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers, who picked up the weekend's most impressive victory.

Before getting to the rankings, there is something very important to keep in mind about our Top 10. It is a Judgement Free Zone! When ranking teams, we do NOT consider any preseason polls or any past season results. What happened in the past is, firmly, in the past.

For instance, you won't find on here … Georgia (it played Tennessee State!) or Ohio State (it played Ball State!). This system normally rewards teams with tougher early-season opponents, but it also makes for an unusual group in the first few weeks. By midseason, our Top 10 may not be much different than many others.

LSU and coach Lane Kiffin drubbed Clemson so much that, somehow, the focus nationally seemed to switch from Kiffin's rousing debut to Dabo Swinney's uncertain future (it would cost Clemson around $50 million to fire him, by the way). But back to the Tigers from Baton Rouge. They're fast, big and tough, and they've finally got a run game in Red Stick, which has been missing now for years. LSU topped 300 yards rushing, much of it from Wisconsin transfer Dilin Jones, a redshirt sophomore who averaged 5 yards a carry and scored twice. LSU barely edged Miami for the most convincing win over a power league opponent in Week 1, which puts them atop our rankings.

That defense everyone's been talking about all offseason showed up in impressive fashion against the Badgers. Five of Wisconsin's eight drives ended in punts and UW managed just 284 yards of offense. LB Drayk Bowen & Co. had a field day against a Wisconsin team that moves slow. Notre Dame didn't allow a run of longer than seven yards. But enough about the defense! Carr, the second-year starter and the grandson of former Michigan coach Lloyd Carr, was a steady 19-of-29 for 239 yards and two touchdowns. It's no secret that Notre Dame is pouring resources into its football roster — and it's showing.

In his debut at QB, Darian Mensah, at his third school in three years, torched the Cardinal with plenty of help from Malachi Toney, the slippery wideout who racked up 234 yards, three touchdowns and surged into the Heisman conversation after just one week. Don't slouch on this victory. Miami traveled across the country (the U got there two days early to acclimate to the time zone) and played on a sleepy Friday night. It had the makings for one of those sleep-walk affairs that we've seen from some of Mario Cristobal's teams. But the reigning runner-ups took care of business quickly (it was 28-3 midway through the second quarter).

Remember that February court battle playing out in Mississippi over Trinidad Chambliss' tonsils? Well, it was well worth it. Chambliss, one of the Heisman Trophy favorites this year, passed for 336 yards, three touchdowns and another 60 yards on the ground. He led the Rebels down the field on a 44-yard drive that ended with Lucas Carneiro's 48-yard game-winning field goal as time expired. Chambliss hit on an 18-yard completion on third-and-6 during that haul and he ran a few times, too. After a duel against Charlotte next week, the Rebels host their former coach in Oxford.

Look, this was no dominant performance by the Ducks. In fact, the Broncos led at halftime and Oregon needed Dakorien Moore to turn a 10-yard completion into a 62-yard touchdown in the final minutes to break a tie game and deliver the win. However, keep in mind that this Boise team might well be a playoff contender as one of the Group of Six's best programs. The Ducks lost three starters on last year's offensive line and it showed. That'll need some improving against a nasty Big Ten schedule that includes USC, Ohio State and Michigan.

The Cavaliers picked up where they left off from last season's 11-3 mark. It didn't seem to matter that they were breaking in a new QB. Former Penn State and Missouri passer/runner Beau Pribula mounted 110 yards rushing and 155 in the air with two scores. Cavs defensive coordinator John Rudzinski's group ran circles around the Wolfpack. NC State didn't score until less than six minutes were left in the third quarter. Given Clemson and FSU's struggles, is UVA the class of the conference behind the Hurricanes? The two programs miss each other during the regular season this year.

The Buffaloes didn't muster much offense (307 yards), but QB Julian Lewis mounted an eight-play, 75-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 20-yard completion to Charlie Williams for the game-winner. It wasn't the finest performance from Coach Prime's crew, but it's enough for the Top 10 — traveling clear across the country in the season opener and controlling the line of scrimmage against what many believed to be one of the ACC's better programs. Speaking of controlling the line of scrimmage, Georgia Tech had 51 yards rushing — a testament to coordinator Chris Marve's unit.

Don't tell coach Alex Golesh we've got his Tigers in the Top 10. He wasn't pleased at all in Auburn's performance against Baylor. In fact, they were mostly outplayed much of the game. If BU quarterback DJ Lagway leads his receiver better on a two-point conversion, the Bears would have completely ruined Golesh's debut. QB Byrum Brown and Auburn's O-line must get better. Brown was sacked five times and threw three interceptions. On the bright side, Auburn's defense forced a few turnovers and stuffed Baylor on some big third downs.

This is a rarity. A Group of Six program that just lost a game finding its way into our Top 10? However, the Broncos showed their stuff in a hostile environment. In fact, we'll learn a lot about the G6 playoff race this coming weekend, when Boise hosts Memphis. And guess what? Boise also travels later in September to Western Michigan, another potential G6 playoff bid candidate. But back to Boise. QB Maddux Madsen — a 27-game starter — threw three touchdown passes and looked fairly sharp, especially in that kind of environment. But Boise's O-line and D-line was the most impressive units on the field.

Surprised to see the Bruins at No. 10? We are too, but this year's season-opening weekend did not afford many power conference-versus-power conference games from which to choose. First-year coach Bob Chesney's debut was a fun one. QB Nico Iamaleava seems like a new man in Chesney's offense. Sure, it wasn't anything prolific (184 yards on 14-of-22 passing), but he didn't make many mistakes. The Bruins got more than 100 yards from Anthony Woods, too. Let's be honest: UCLA is unlikely to hang around our Top 10 for very long, but look for Chesney's group to surprise some folks.

articles.body:
When Jose Mourinho left Inter Milan for Real Madrid in the summer of 2010, after leading the Italian outfit to Champions League glory, he was at the peak of his powers.

The Portuguese coach claimed an historic treble with Inter, clinching Serie A in the last week of the season and lifting the Coppa Italia.

Inter beat Bayern 2-0 in the Champions League final at Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu stadium, winning the trophy for the first time since 1965 and becoming the first Italian team to win the treble.

The day after the final Mourinho said it was likely his last match in charge and around a week later his appointment at Real Madrid was finalised.

Now 16 years on, and beginning his second stint at Madrid, Mourinho kicks off the record 15-time Champions League winners' European campaign against Inter on Tuesday at the Bernabeu.

Neither the veteran coach nor Inter have been able to reproduce that level of European success since.

Inter have reached the final on two subsequent occasions, beaten in 2023 by Manchester City and then thrashed by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 showpiece.

Mourinho was unable to help Real Madrid past the semi-finals and after leaving the club in 2013 has mainly spent his time competing in lower levels of European competition.

The 63-year-old led Manchester United to the Europa League in 2017 and won the Conference League with Roma in 2022.

Fished out of the relative wilderness by Madrid president Florentino Perez this summer after two seasons without a major trophy for Los Blancos, Mourinho's main task is to return the club to their European throne.

Only five coaches have won the trophy more times than Mourinho, who also lifted it with Porto in 2004 to kickstart his career and earn him passage to Chelsea and Europe's biggest leagues.

"My attraction to Real Madrid is due to its history, its frustrations in recent years and its expectations to win," said Mourinho in 2010, although the same holds true now, after a remarkable period of success ended.

In his first reign Mourinho helped disrupt Pep Guardiola's Barcelona's dominance within Spain but was unable to help Madrid end their wait for a 10th European Cup.

That came under his successor Carlo Ancelotti, who claimed three with Madrid over two spells at the club.

Zinedine Zidane also lifted the trophy three times in consecutive seasons, with Madrid winning six in a remarkable 10-year spell.

Perez credits Mourinho with building the foundations for those trophies.

"I'm glad my work had some positive impact, but the titles belong to Carlo, Zidane, the players, and the fans," said Mourinho.

Madrid's grip on the trophy has loosened during the past two years, knocked out in the quarter-finals by Arsenal in 2025 and last season they were eliminated by Bayern Munich in the last 16.

Mourinho's challenge is to prove both he and Real Madrid still can rule among Europe's elite, and stopping Luis Enrique's PSG retaining it for a third year running.

"Finishing without trophies at Real Madrid is not a successful season," said Mourinho in August.

The coach's second stint at Madrid started smoothly with three wins from three games, but on Friday they fell to their first defeat, 1-0 at Real Betis.

Inter's visit to the Spanish capital will be an early test of whether Mourinho can restore Madrid's European fortunes, against the club with which he last reached the pinnacle of the competition.

articles.title: Getafe - Celta | Antes de viajar hay que limpiar la casa: previa, análisis, predicción y pronóstico
articles.standfirst: Mal inicio de dos equipos que juegan en Europa
articles.summary: Mal inicio de dos equipos que juegan en Europa
articles.body: El Getafe arranca un periplo de cuatro partidos en apenas trece días en el que los azulones buscarán escalar posiciones en la tabla y amarrar un buen puñado de puntos de cara al objetivo de la permanencia marcada por el conjunto azulón después de un mal inicio. Tampoco ha empezado mejor el Celta, otro de nuestros representantes en competición europea, que necesita sumar puntos antes de que empiece la Europa League para no meterse en un jaleo. Cómo llega el Getafe: El Getafe recibe al Celta para cerrar la cuarta jornada de competición. Los azulones, que perdieron el pasado lunes frente a Osasuna, buscan tres puntos que hagan a los de Bordalás respirar en la tabla. Los del sur de Madrid tan solo suman un triunfo en las tres primeras fechas y quieren volver a sumar con otra victoria en el Coliseum, donde ya vencieron en liga al Racing y en Conference al Partizán. Cómo llega el Celta: Busca el Celta continuar consiguiendo buenos resultados a domicilio, a ser posible con la primera victoria de la temporada y que no se repita el mal inicio de la pasada campaña. Borja Iglesias, ya con el alta médica, y el recién llegado, Sebastián Cáceres, son las dos principales novedades de la convocatoria. Lista en la que no se encuentra Faye, uno de los fichajes de esta temporada, por decisión técnica, y Aleix Febas, que continúa lesionado. El duelo del partido: Enes Ünal vs Jutglà. Getafe y Celta suman un gol cada uno en LaLiga, una cifra demasiado pobre como para pensar en intentar cumplir ningún objetivo. Por eso los dos delanteros titulares tendrán el foco sobre ellos para intentar engordar esas malas estadísticas de inicio de curso.

articles.title: El Aston Villa, el más beneficiado del auge del mercado árabe
articles.standfirst: El equipo inglés encabeza la lista de equipos que más dinero han ingresado por ventas a la liga saudí
articles.summary: El equipo inglés encabeza la lista de equipos que más dinero han ingresado por ventas a la liga saudí
articles.body: Desde hace unos años, el mercado árabe ha irrumpido con fuerza en el panorama del fútbol mundial. Grandes estrellas y promesas han preferido marcharse a jugar a Arabia Saudí antes que competir en la élite europea. Algunos de los casos de este verano han sido el de Tijjani Reijnders, centrocampista neerlandés que ha llegado a la liga tras solo una temporada después de llegar al City o el de Ollie Watkins, medalla de bronce en el Mundial con Inglaterra y deseado por varios equipos de la Premier. Aunque los beneficiados no solo son los jugadores que llegan para recibir grandes salarios. También los clubes que reciben una gran cantidad de dinero por el traspaso de sus figuras. La llegada de Cristiano fue un punto de inflexión, y Neymar marcó el récord aún a superar. El brasileño dejó el PSG por Al-Hilal en 2023 a cambio de 90 millones de euros, el traspaso más caro de la historia de la liga. Y hay equipos que se han visto muy beneficiados. Principalmente de la Premier League. Seis entidades inglesas entran en el top 10 de clubes que más dinero han recibido por traspasos a la liga saudí. El que encabeza la lista es el Aston Villa con tres ventas. Estas son Jhon Durán por 77 millones de euros, Moussa Diaby por 60 y Ollie Watkins por 58,4. El segundo puesto lo tiene el Manchester City, gracias a la venta de Tijjani Reijnders, por 61 millones de euros. A él se suman Riyad Mahrez por 35, Aymeric Laporte por 27,5 y Joao Cancelo por 25. El equipo que cierra el podio también es otro de Premier, el Liverpool, con las salidas de Darwin Núñez por 53 millones, Fabinho por 46,7 y Jordan Henderson por 14. Sin duda, la temporada 23/24 fue la que comenzó todo. En ella, llegaron a la liga 19 de los 50 fichajes más caros que se han dado hasta el momento. Sin embargo, cada año se suman a la liga nuevos jugadores que entran directos a la lista de traspasos más caros. En esta ventana han entrado al top 5 dos futbolistas, Gabriel Martinelli y Crysencio Summerville, que han llegado ambos a Al-Hilal por 70 y 64,5 millones de euros respectivamente. Hay tres clubes que han sido los grandes inversores para que estas estrellas hayan llegado a la liga, aunque el resto también se está reforzando en cierta medida. El club que ostenta el traspaso más caro es a su vez el que más dinero ha invertido. Desde la 23/24, Al-Hilal se ha gastado 856,99 millones de euros en incorporaciones, de los cuales 632,84 han ido directos para equipos de las cinco grandes ligas. Mientras que en ventas, tan solo ha sumado 48,59 millones de euros a sus arcas. Le sigue Al-Nassr, el conjunto de Cristiano Ronaldo, con un total de 436,83 millones invertidos y solo 42,14 recuperados. El podio lo cierra Al-Ittihad, muy cerca de los segundos con 414,18 millones gastados y 40,13 ingresados.
